items.contents:
Language focus:
 - Vocabulary: leisure activities (doing DIY, knitting, building dollhouses, making paper flowers, cycling, playing sports, messaging friends, surfing the net, cooking, doing puzzles); expressions of likes/dislikes (like, love, enjoy, prefer).
 Skill focus:
 - Listening
 - Reading
 - Speaking
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Identify and use vocabulary related to leisure activities.
 - Describe favourite leisure activities using simple expressions.
 - Ask and answer questions about free-time activities.
 Skills:
 - Listening: identify the main ideas and specific information in a conversation about leisure activities.
 - Reading: understand the main ideas and specific information in a conversation about leisure activities.
 - Speaking: talk about personal leisure activities with classmates.
 Value:
 - [Respect] Appreciate and respect different hobbies and interests of others.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Listen and repeat the target vocabulary.
 - Match the words with pictures of free-time activities.
 Core group:
 - Read the conversation and complete the True/False activity.
 - Complete the gap-fill activity using information from the conversation.
 Challenge group:
 - Name additional free-time activities not mentioned in the textbook.
 - Interview a partner about favourite free-time activities and report the findings.
items.assess:
- Vocabulary matching activity.
 - Pair discussion.
 - Teacher observation checklist.
 - Exit ticket: write three leisure activities and one favourite activity.

items.contents:
Language focus:
 - Vocabulary collocations (be interested in, be keen on, be fond of, be crazy about, be into).
 - Pronunciation: /ʊ/ and /uː/.
 Skill focus:
- Listening
- Speaking
- Writing
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Use vocabulary and collocations to express preferences.
 - Pronounce /ʊ/ and /uː/ accurately in words and sentences.
 Skills:
 - Listening: distinguish /ʊ/ and /uː/ in words and sentences about leisure activities.
- Speaking: pronounce the target sounds accurately and use preference collocations to talk about likes and dislikes.
- Writing: complete and write short sentences about personal leisure preferences using the target collocations.
 Value:
 - [Confidence] Communicate clearly and confidently.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Match pictures with vocabulary words.
 - Complete sentences using the target vocabulary.
 Core group:
 - Categorise leisure activities into indoor and outdoor groups.
 - Practise pronunciation by reading target words and sentences with a partner.
 Challenge group:
 - Expand the vocabulary list with more leisure activities.
 - Create short conversations using the target vocabulary and pronunciation naturally.
items.assess:
- Vocabulary completion.
 - Pronunciation practice.
 - Oral performance checklist.
 - Teacher feedback.

items.contents:
Language focus:
 - Grammar: verbs of liking/disliking + gerunds; verbs of liking/disliking + to-infinitives.
 Skill focus:
- Reading
- Writing
- Speaking
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Express likes, dislikes and preferences using appropriate grammatical structures.
 - Apply target grammar in meaningful communication.
 Skills:
- Reading: identify which verbs of liking and disliking are followed by gerunds, to-infinitives or both forms.
- Writing: complete and produce sentences using the correct verb patterns after verbs of liking and disliking.
- Speaking: ask and answer questions about leisure preferences using gerunds and to-infinitives accurately.
 Value:
 - [Self-expression] Express personal opinions politely and confidently.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Complete guided grammar exercises using sentence frames.
 - Choose the correct verb forms after verbs of liking.
 Core group:
 - Complete multiple-choice grammar activities.
 - Interview a partner about free-time activities using verbs of liking and write the answers.
 Challenge group:
 - Write original sentences using different verbs of liking.
 - Conduct a class survey and report classmates' preferences using the target grammar.
items.assess:
- Grammar exercises.
 - Sentence completion.
 - Pair speaking assessment.
 - Teacher observation and immediate feedback.

items.contents:
Language focus:
 - Reading text: The Zebras of La Paz - young traffic wardens and the personal qualities needed for the job.
 - Reading strategy: understanding the whole text and matching sentences to gaps.
 Skill focus:
 - Reading
 - Speaking
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Understand a factual article about an unusual job and the qualities required to do it well.
 - Use context and text cohesion to place missing sentences accurately.
 Skills:
 - Reading: identify the main idea, follow references and match sentences to gaps in The Zebras of La Paz.
 - Speaking: discuss suitable personal qualities for different jobs and justify opinions.
 Value:
 - [Confidence] Recognise personal strengths and speak positively about abilities.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Preview the title, photos and key vocabulary before reading.
 - Use a paragraph-by-paragraph organiser to track people, places and reference words.
 Core group:
 - Complete the gapped-text task and underline evidence for each answer.
 - Compare answers and discuss which qualities make an effective traffic warden.
 Challenge group:
 - Explain why the distractor sentences do not fit each gap.
 - Summarise the article and evaluate whether the job would suit them.
items.assess:
- Reading comprehension and gapped-text answers.
 - Evidence-underlining check.
 - Pair-discussion observation.

items.contents:
Language focus:
 - Vocabulary: jobs - actor, architect, astronaut, athlete, camera operator, chef, firefighter, hairdresser, lawyer, librarian, politician and soldier.
 - Personality adjectives used to describe suitability for work.
 Skill focus:
 - Reading
 - Speaking
 - Writing
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Use job nouns and personality adjectives accurately in context.
 - Describe the qualities needed for selected careers.
 Skills:
 - Reading: use definitions and sentence context to identify jobs and personality adjectives.
 - Speaking: discuss which qualities are important for different jobs.
 - Writing: complete and create sentences that connect people, jobs and personal qualities.
 Value:
 - [Self-awareness] Identify personal qualities that can support future learning and work.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Match job words to pictures or definitions using a word bank.
 - Complete sentence frames such as A firefighter needs to be....
 Core group:
 - Complete the vocabulary tasks and compare choices in pairs.
 - Write and share descriptions of three jobs using suitable adjectives.
 Challenge group:
 - Distinguish closely related personality adjectives and justify word choice.
 - Create a short career profile for an unusual job using precise vocabulary.
items.assess:
- Vocabulary matching and sentence completion.
 - Job-description sentences.
 - Teacher questioning.

items.contents:
Language focus:
 - Grammar: present simple and present continuous.
 - Stative verbs and verbs that can change meaning in continuous forms.
 Skill focus:
 - Reading
 - Speaking
 - Writing
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Choose between present simple and present continuous according to meaning and time reference.
 - Use common stative verbs accurately.
 Skills:
 - Reading: identify time expressions and contextual clues that signal the required tense.
 - Speaking: describe routines and actions happening around now.
 - Writing: complete and produce accurate sentences with present tenses and stative verbs.
 Value:
 - [Accuracy] Check meaning and time reference before choosing a verb form.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Use a tense timeline and colour-code routines, temporary actions and states.
 - Complete guided sentences with the verb already provided.
 Core group:
 - Complete the textbook grammar tasks and explain choices to a partner.
 - Write paired sentences contrasting a routine with a current temporary action.
 Challenge group:
 - Explain verbs that can be stative or dynamic depending on meaning.
 - Create an error-correction task using present tenses.
items.assess:
- Grammar exercise accuracy.
 - Personalised present-tense sentences.
 - Teacher observation of explanations.

items.contents:
Language focus:
 - Listening strategy: choosing the correct picture and checking every visual detail.
 - Exam task: multiple choice with picture options in short conversations about people, work and plans.
 Skill focus:
 - Reading
 - Listening
 - Speaking
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Identify key details that distinguish similar picture options.
 - Use prediction and elimination strategies before and during listening.
 Skills:
 - Reading: analyse picture options and predict the words or details that may be heard.
 - Listening: identify specific information and select the picture that matches each conversation.
 - Speaking: compare answers and explain which detail confirmed the choice.
 Value:
 - [Attentiveness] Listen carefully before making a decision.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Name the visible differences between the pictures before listening.
 - Listen in short sections and tick key details on a visual checklist.
 Core group:
 - Complete the picture-based listening task and compare evidence in pairs.
 - Explain the difference between the correct picture and one distractor.
 Challenge group:
 - Predict paraphrases for each picture before listening.
 - Write and perform a short conversation that matches a new picture set.
items.assess:
- Picture-option listening score.
 - Key-detail checklist.
 - Oral explanation of answers.

items.contents:
Language focus:
- Employment vocabulary: candidate, full-time, part-time, retired, qualification and unemployed.
- Life events and work or education phrases: get married, grow up, go to university or college, go out with someone, split up with someone, be out of work, be brought up by someone and apply for a job.
Skill focus:
- Reading
- Listening
- Speaking
- Writing
items.outcomes:
Language use:
- Use employment vocabulary accurately to describe work status and qualifications.
- Sequence important life, education and work events clearly.
Skills:
- Reading: use definitions and context to identify employment words and life-event phrases.
- Listening: identify and order key events in a person’s life story.
- Speaking: describe a person’s education, work and life events in chronological order.
- Writing: complete and produce accurate sentences using the target vocabulary and phrases.
Value:
- [Respect] Recognise that people may follow different education, work and life paths.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Use a labelled timeline and match employment terms to simple definitions.
 - Reorder model life events before listening or speaking.
 Core group:
 - Complete the vocabulary and sequencing tasks.
 - Interview a partner about education, skills and possible future jobs.
 Challenge group:
 - Use the target vocabulary to create a detailed future career pathway.
 - Compare formal employment terms with everyday alternatives.
items.assess:
- Vocabulary completion.
 - Ordered listening timeline.
 - Partner interview notes.

items.contents:
Language focus:
 - Speaking: talking about life, family, education and future plans.
 - Exam strategy: giving detailed answers in an interview.
 Skill focus:
 - Reading
 - Listening
 - Speaking
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Answer personal interview questions with relevant detail.
 - Extend responses using reasons, examples and linking expressions.
 Skills:
 - Reading: interpret interview prompts and useful-language frames.
 - Listening: identify how model speakers extend and clarify their answers.
 - Speaking: maintain an interview, answer follow-up questions and use clear pronunciation.
 Value:
 - [Confidence] Communicate personal information clearly and respectfully.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Use question cards and answer frames with because, but and also.
 - Rehearse answers with a supportive partner before the interview.
 Core group:
 - Conduct a paired interview and ask at least one follow-up question.
 - Use the speaking checklist to improve detail and clarity.
 Challenge group:
 - Respond to unexpected follow-up questions without written preparation.
 - Act as interviewer and give specific feedback on detail, fluency and interaction.
items.assess:
- Interview speaking rubric.
 - Peer feedback checklist.
 - Teacher observation.

items.contents:
Language Focus:
- Key vocabulary: dissolving, solute, solvent, solution, transparent and opaque.
- Formation and basic properties of a solution.
- Particle explanation of dissolving.
- Differences between transparent, colourless and opaque substances.
- Sentence patterns for making predictions, describing observations and giving evidence.
Skills Focus:
- Reading
- Speaking
- Writing
items.sb:
Resources:
- Open the Teacher Guide first for the teaching flow and materials.
- Use the Student Handout during the lesson and refer to the Teacher Handout for source content.
- Teachers may flexibly adapt the Teacher Guide and Student Handout to suit students while maintaining the learning outcomes and safety requirements.

Week 1_Unit 2.1_Dissolving
items.outcomes:
Language Use:
- Define and use dissolving, solute, solvent, solution, transparent and opaque accurately.
- Identify the solute and solvent in a solution.
- Describe how a solution forms using particle theory.
- Explain why a transparent solution does not have to be colourless.
- Use observations as evidence to decide whether a mixture is a solution.
Skills:
- Reading: identify key definitions and information in short Science texts and diagrams.
- Speaking: discuss predictions and explain observations using complete Science sentences.
- Writing: complete particle explanations and write evidence-based answers.
Value:
- Develop curiosity and accuracy when observing and identifying solutions.
items.activities:
Support group:
- Provide a word bank, labelled particle diagrams and sentence frames.
- Allow students to use completed guided notes before writing explanations.
- Model one prediction and observation sentence.
Core group:
- Complete all vocabulary, demonstration and particle-model activities.
- Create a one-page explanation of how a solution forms.
- Use peer feedback to improve the explanation.
Challenge group:
- Explain why the colour of copper sulfate shows that the solute is still present.
- Explain why milk is not a solution despite being a liquid mixture.
items.assess:
- Prior-knowledge discussion and particle drawing.
- Vocabulary matching task.
- Prediction and observation table.
- Particle-model explanation.
- Peer-assessed one-page explanation.
- Check-your-understanding questions.
- Exit Ticket.

items.contents:
Language focus:
- Grammar: countable and uncountable nouns.
- Quantifiers and quantity expressions: some, any, many, much, a lot of, lots of, a few, a little, a number of and a kilo of.
Skill focus:
- Reading
- Speaking
- Writing
items.outcomes:
Language use:
- Distinguish countable and uncountable nouns accurately.
- Select suitable quantifiers and quantity expressions according to the noun and context.
Skills:
- Reading: use sentence context to identify countable and uncountable nouns and suitable quantifiers.
- Speaking: ask and answer questions about people, food and quantities using the target structures.
- Writing: complete and produce accurate sentences with countable and uncountable nouns and quantifiers.
Value:
- [Accuracy] Use quantity expressions carefully and appropriately in communication.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Sort example nouns into a guided countable/uncountable table.
 - Use quantifier sentence frames and visual quantity cues.
 Core group:
 - Complete the grammar tasks and explain choices in pairs.
 - Write and exchange a short quantity questionnaire.
 Challenge group:
 - Explain nouns that can be countable or uncountable with different meanings.
 - Create and correct a paragraph containing quantifier errors.
items.assess:
- Noun-classification table.
 - Quantifier exercise accuracy.
 - Personalised question-and-answer task.

items.contents:
Language focus:
 - Live well, study well: being a team player and having confidence in yourself.
 - Useful language for teamwork, encouragement and sharing ideas.
 Skill focus:
 - Reading
 - Speaking
 - Writing
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Identify behaviours that help a team work effectively.
 - Reflect on personal strengths and set one teamwork goal.
 Skills:
 - Reading: understand advice and scenarios about confidence and teamwork.
 - Speaking: discuss team roles, offer encouragement and solve a simple group challenge.
 - Writing: record strengths, team contributions and a realistic improvement target.
 Value:
 - [Teamwork] Contribute responsibly and encourage others during group work.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Use role cards and a teamwork-language bank.
 - Choose strengths from a list and complete guided reflection prompts.
 Core group:
 - Complete the teamwork tasks and agree on fair roles for a group challenge.
 - Write one specific teamwork target and action step.
 Challenge group:
 - Lead the group challenge while ensuring every member contributes.
 - Evaluate two different teamwork strategies and recommend the most effective one.
items.assess:
- Teamwork observation checklist.
 - Completed reflection and action target.
 - Peer feedback on participation.

 Skill focus:

items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Analyse an email task and include every required content point.
 - Write a clear, organised informal email of about 100 words.
 Skills:
 - Reading: identify required content, informal expressions and paragraph organisation in a model email.
 - Writing: plan, draft and edit an informal email using appropriate register and accurate unit language.
 Value:
 - [Consideration] Communicate warmly and include the information another person needs.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Highlight each content point in the task and use a paragraph frame.
 - Use a bank of informal greetings, linkers and closing phrases.
 Core group:
 - Plan the email, write a first draft and peer-check all content points.
 - Revise grammar, spelling, punctuation and paragraphing before submission.
 Challenge group:
 - Improve cohesion and natural informal style without adding irrelevant information.
 - Give precise peer feedback linked to the exam-task criteria.
items.assess:

 - Final informal email.

Week 2_Unit 2.1_Dissolving, melting and mass
items.outcomes:
Language Use:
- Distinguish dissolving from melting using accurate examples.
- Use solute, solvent, solution and conserved correctly.
- Record and report mass measurements using g.
- Explain that the solute remains present after dissolving.
- State a conclusion about conservation of mass using practical evidence.

- Listening: follow practical instructions and safety guidance accurately.
- Speaking: compare dissolving and melting and discuss practical results.

- Complete the practical measurements and calculations accurately.
- Explain conservation of mass using measured evidence.
Challenge group:
- Explain how spilling or losing material would affect the final mass.
- Suggest ways to improve the accuracy of the investigation.
- Distinguish clearly between an observation, result, conclusion and explanation.
items.assess:

- Dissolving and melting classification.
- Practical measurement and calculation record.
- Conservation-of-mass explanation.

- Summary Checklist.
- Exit Ticket.

- Reading: Analyse picture details, captions and answer options before listening.
- Speaking: Compare answers and explain which details support each picture choice.
Value:
- [Focused listening] Listen attentively for complete and accurate information.
items.activities:
Support group:
- Identify and describe the main differences between the picture options before listening.
- Use a short vocabulary list and guided questions to predict possible answers.
Core group:
- Analyse the picture options, complete the listening task and compare evidence in pairs.
- Explain which words or details in the recording support each selected answer.
Challenge group:
- Predict possible distractors and explain why they may be misleading.
- Retell one short conversation using the information shown in the correct picture.
items.assess:
- Picture-option listening task accuracy.
- Oral explanation of answer choices.
- Teacher observation of prediction and listening strategies.

items.contents:

- Contextual use of descriptive language for activities and experiences.
Skill Focus:
- Reading
- Writing
- Speaking
items.outcomes:
Language Use:
- Recognise and use common phrasal verbs related to free-time activities.
- Use suitable adjectives to describe activities, experiences and personal reactions.
Skills:
- Reading: Use definitions and sentence context to identify suitable phrasal verbs and descriptive adjectives.
- Writing: Complete and produce sentences using accurate phrasal verbs and adjectives.
- Speaking: Describe a free-time activity or experience using the target vocabulary.
Value:
- [Purposeful leisure] Appreciate positive and meaningful ways of using free time.
items.activities:
Support group:
- Match phrasal verbs and adjectives with simple definitions or pictures.
- Complete controlled sentences using a word bank and highlighted contextual clues.
Core group:
- Complete the vocabulary exercises independently and compare answers in pairs.
- Write and share sentences describing a chosen free-time experience.
Challenge group:
- Explain differences between similar adjectives and correct unsuitable phrasal verbs in context.
- Give a detailed spoken description of a memorable activity using varied target vocabulary.
items.assess:
- Phrasal-verb and adjective task accuracy.
- Written sentences using the target vocabulary.
- Short oral description of a free-time experience.

items.contents:
Language focus:
 - Reading: A text about the possibility of life on other planets and the conditions needed for planets to support human life.
 - Speaking: Talking about the conditions needed for a planet to support human life.
 Skill focus:
 - Reading
 - Speaking
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Identify information about the conditions needed for planets to support human life.
 - Use vocabulary related to space and planets to discuss scientific ideas.
 - Express and justify opinions about whether a planet can support human life.
 Skills:
 - Reading: identify the main ideas and specific information in the text about the possibility of life on other planets and the conditions needed for planets to support human life.
 - Speaking: discuss the conditions required for a planet to support human life and explain personal opinions clearly.
 Value:
 - [Scientific Curiosity] Develop curiosity about space exploration while appreciating scientific evidence when discussing life on other planets.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Match highlighted vocabulary with their meanings before reading.
 - Highlight key information in the text to identify the conditions needed for human life.
 Core group:
 - Complete a graphic organiser summarising the conditions for a habitable planet.
 - Discuss with a partner which condition is the most important and explain the reasons.
 Challenge group:
 - Compare Mars with Earth using evidence from the reading passage.
 - Debate whether humans will be able to live on another planet in the future, supporting opinions with evidence.
items.assess:
- Reading comprehension checklist.
 - Speaking observation.
 - Teacher feedback.
 - Exit ticket.

items.contents:
Language focus:
 - Listening: A student talking about an imaginary planet called Planet Hope and its creatures (Hopeans).
 - Writing: Write a paragraph (80–100 words) describing imaginary creatures living on another planet.
 Skill focus:
 - Listening
 - Writing
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Identify key information about Planet Hope and the Hopeans.
 - Write a well-organised paragraph (80–100 words) describing imaginary creatures living on another planet.
 Skills:
 - Listening: identify specific information in the talk about Planet Hope and complete listening tasks accurately.
 - Writing: organise ideas logically, describe the creatures' appearance, behaviour and lifestyle, and revise writing based on feedback.
 Value:
 - [Creativity] Develop imagination by designing original creatures while applying appropriate language accurately.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Match key vocabulary with pictures before listening.
 - Complete a guided note-taking worksheet while listening.
 Core group:
 - Compare listening answers with a partner before class discussion.
 - Write the paragraph using the provided planning table and revise it through peer feedback.
 Challenge group:
 - Extend the paragraph by adding interesting details about the creatures' abilities and habitat.
 - Exchange writing with classmates and provide constructive feedback using a writing checklist.
items.assess:

 - Writing rubric.
 - Peer feedback checklist.
 - Teacher observation.

items.contents:

 - Review pronunciation: Intonation for making lists.
 - Review grammar: Reported speech (questions).
 - Project: Our Favourite Planet – Choose a planet in the solar system, research information about it (name, size, atmosphere, temperature, appearance and special features), design a poster and present it to the class.

- Writing
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Consolidate vocabulary, pronunciation and grammar from Unit 12.
 - Present information about a planet using appropriate vocabulary and language structures.
 Skills:
- Speaking: discuss researched information about a chosen planet, present important facts and respond to classmates’ questions.
- Writing: organise information about the planet’s position, size, atmosphere, temperature, appearance and special features.
 Value:
 - [Exploration] Develop interest in astronomy and space exploration through collaborative research and presentation.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Review vocabulary and reported questions through matching and guided practice.
 - Complete a project planning sheet using teacher-provided guiding questions.
 Core group:
 - Work in groups to design a poster introducing a planet in the solar system.
 - Present the poster and exchange peer feedback using a presentation checklist.

items.outcomes:

Support group:

 Core group:

items.assess:

items.contents:
Language focus:
 - Reading: Three notices about a science club, a school speaking contest and a talk about future means of communication.
 - Speaking: Ask and answer about a device or an app used for studying, then report a partner’s answers to the class.
 - Listening: A talk about the solar system.
 - Writing: Write a paragraph (80–100 words) about your favourite means of communication.
 Skill focus:
 - Reading
 - Speaking
 - Listening
 - Writing
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Apply vocabulary and grammar from Units 10–12 in integrated language tasks.
 - Express ideas clearly using appropriate language in familiar contexts.
 Skills:
 - Reading: identify specific information in three notices about a science club, a school speaking contest and a talk about future means of communication.
 - Speaking: ask and answer questions about a device or an app used for studying and report a partner's ideas clearly.
 - Listening: identify specific information in a talk about the solar system and complete listening tasks accurately.
 - Writing: write a well-organised paragraph (80–100 words) about a favourite means of communication, explaining how often it is used, its benefits and future use.
 Value:
 - [Digital Citizenship & Scientific Curiosity] Develop responsible communication habits while showing curiosity about science, technology and space exploration.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Highlight key information in each notice and complete a guided reading organiser.
 - Use a writing frame and a vocabulary bank to complete the writing task.
 Core group:
 - Compare reading and listening answers with a partner before class discussion.
 - Conduct a pair interview about a study app or device and use the responses to draft the writing task.
 Challenge group:
 - Create two higher-order comprehension questions based on one of the notices and discuss them with classmates.
 - Extend the writing by comparing different means of communication and explaining which one is most suitable for different situations.
items.assess:
- Reading comprehension checklist.
 - Listening checklist.
 - Speaking observation.
 - Writing rubric.
 - Peer feedback checklist.

items.contents:
Language focus:
 - Speaking: listening carefully to the question and answering fully.
 - Elaboration questions for extending a general conversation about free time.
 Skill focus:
 - Reading
 - Listening
 - Speaking
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Respond directly to free-time questions and add relevant detail.
 - Use elaboration questions and follow-up to sustain interaction.
 Skills:
 - Reading: interpret prompts and useful-language examples.
 - Listening: identify the exact focus of questions and effective extended responses.
 - Speaking: give relevant answers, add reasons or examples and ask follow-up questions.
 Value:
 - [Interest in others] Listen carefully and respond to what another person actually says.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Underline the key word in each question and use answer-expansion frames.
 - Practise with predictable question-and-follow-up cards.
 Core group:
 - Complete a paired general conversation and use at least two elaboration questions.
 - Use peer feedback to improve relevance, detail and interaction.
 Challenge group:
 - Respond naturally to spontaneous questions and link ideas across answers.
 - Lead a conversation that demonstrates active listening and balanced participation.
items.assess:
- General-conversation rubric.
 - Question-focus and elaboration checklist.
 - Peer and teacher feedback.

items.contents:

 Skill focus:

 - Writing
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Understand the main ideas and details in a video about table games in a public space.
 - Discuss how shared activities can build community and use free time positively.
 Skills:
 - Reading: preview questions and key activity vocabulary.
 - Listening: identify participants, rules, equipment and opinions while viewing.
 - Speaking: compare games and discuss inclusive community activities.

 Value:

items.contents:
Language focus:
 - Writing: an article about free-time activities.
 - Using linking words and phrases, adding details and maintaining an engaging style.
 Skill focus:
 - Reading
 - Writing
items.outcomes:
Language use:
 - Analyse how a model article develops ideas and engages the reader.
 - Write an organised article with relevant detail and varied linking language.
 Skills:
 - Reading: identify title, paragraph focus, linking expressions and supporting detail in a model article.
 - Writing: plan, draft and edit an article that answers the task and develops each idea clearly.
 Value:
 - [Balanced lifestyle] Encourage positive and responsible use of free time.
items.activities:
Support group:
 - Use a paragraph plan and a linking-word bank grouped by function.
 - Expand each main point with a reason, example or personal detail.
 Core group:
 - Write the article and peer-check organisation, relevance and detail.
 - Revise repeated language, linking and accuracy before submission.
 Challenge group:
 - Use a lively but appropriate style and varied cohesive devices.
 - Give detailed editorial feedback on development, reader interest and cohesion.
items.assess:
- Article plan.
 - Final free-time article.
 - Writing rubric and reflection checklist.
